_comment: Ten EU and UK institutional feeds. Tier 1 sources get a small scoring bonus over tier 2. Scope is deliberately EU + UK only. EUR-Lex was removed on 24 Aug 2026: it returns 403 to GitHub's runners. The European Parliament feed is retained but returns empty to them for the same reason.

sources.name: Council of the EU — external relations documents
sources.note: Replaces EUR-Lex, which refuses GitHub's servers. Primary Council documents - decisions, regulations, conclusions - in the external relations file, which is where sanctions law lives. Titles arrive as document codes, so the parser swaps in the descriptive subject line.

sources.name: Council of the EU — press releases
sources.note: Where sanctions packages are actually adopted. Carries some French-language items; the noise list drops them.

sources.name: European Parliament — press releases
sources.note: Committee stages, votes and trilogue outcomes - the in-progress pipeline.

sources.name: OFSI — financial sanctions (HM Treasury)
sources.note: General licences, designations, enforcement. The single best UK sanctions source.

sources.name: FCDO — sanctions and foreign policy
sources.note: UK designations and the Sanctions List updates.

sources.name: Department for Business and Trade
sources.note: Export controls, trade remedies, and UKCA/CE marking - the divergence beat's UK end.

sources.name: gov.uk — news and communications
sources.note: Broad catch-all across departments. High volume, so the filter does the work.

sources.name: DEFRA — food, farming and biosecurity
sources.note: SPS checks and the border target operating model - the sharpest edge of EU-UK divergence. Same gov.uk pattern as the other four, but unconfirmed; check the health table.
